data.gender_notes: Hijaab is used as a unisex name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: A term used in Islamic tradition to refer to the practice of covering the head and chest of women as a sign of modesty and submission to God. The name Hijaab carries the meaning “Covering, Protection” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic. Parents who choose Hijaab usually hope their child will grow to embody covering, protection and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Hijaab total 4, giving a life-path number of 4. Number 4 is linked with Rahu and with the qualities of stability, discipline and hard work.

in_english.name: Hijaab
in_english.meaning: A garment or veil worn by Muslim women
in_english.long_meaning: Hijaab is derived from the Arabic root 'hajaba', meaning to cover or veil. In Islamic tradition, hijaab refers to the head and body covering worn by Muslim women as a symbol of modesty and piety. The concept of hijaab is rooted in Quranic teachings, specifically in Surah An-Nur (Chapter 24, Verse 31) and Surah Al-A'raf (Chapter 7, Verse 26), which instruct women to cover their bodies and lower their gaze. Hijaab is not just a physical covering but also a spiritual symbol of a woman's devotion to her faith and her commitment to maintaining her dignity and honor.

data.cultural_impact: The hijaab is a symbol of a woman's commitment to her faith and cultural identity as a Muslim. It is a visible sign of her adherence to Islamic values and has become an important aspect of Muslim women's expression of their religious and cultural beliefs. In some Muslim communities, wearing the hijaab is seen as a sign of respect for the religious and moral values of Islam and is an important part of maintaining a strong Muslim identity.
data.spiritual_significance: The hijaab holds deep spiritual significance for many Muslim women as it is seen as a way to fulfill the command of God to cover one's awrah (privacy) in public. The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) said, "O young girls, you must watch your dress, behave properly in the presence of men and not let your clothes be a source of curiosity for them." (Bukhari) By wearing the hijaab, women are not only fulfilling this religious requirement but also practicing self-control and modesty - values highly promoted in Islam. In addition, the hijaab can serve as a constant reminder of one's relationship with God and the importance of maintaining a strong spiritual connection.
